context: A tutor discusses a research project on urban green spaces with two students.

sub_blocks.word_limit: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER

lines.text: Now turn to Section Three. You will hear a tutor and two students discussing a research project.

Questions twenty-one to twenty-four. Complete the flowchart below. Write no more than two words and/or a number for each answer. First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-four.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-four.
So, Priya, Tom — how's the research project on urban green spaces coming along?
Good, I think. We've finished the literature review, and we're planning the survey now.
Good. And what's the main focus going to be?
We want to look at how access to parks affects residents' reported stress levels.
Interesting. How many participants are you aiming for?
We're hoping for around one hundred and fifty, across three different neighbourhoods.
And how many neighbourhoods did you say, again?
Three — we wanted a mix of areas with very different levels of green space.
That's a sensible design. And when is this all due?
We've only got six weeks left before the deadline, so it's fairly tight.
Questions twenty-five to twenty-seven. Complete the summary below. Write one word only for each answer. First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-five to twenty-seven.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-five to twenty-seven.
Now, Tom, is there anything you're particularly worried about with the project so far?
Honestly, it's the timeline that worries me most — six weeks doesn't feel like much.
And Priya, is it the same for you, or something else?
For me it's more about the sample — making sure we're not just surveying people who already use the parks a lot.
Understood. Let's arrange a check-in before then — shall we say a fortnight from now?
A fortnight works well for us, yes.
Questions twenty-eight to thirty. Complete the notes below. Write no more than two words for each answer. First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-eight to thirty.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-eight to thirty.
Fair point. Now, who's taking the methodology section for the write-up?
That's mine — I'll write up the methodology.
And the literature review?
I've got that one, along with the discussion section at the end.
So who's handling the discussion section, just to confirm?
That's me as well.
Great, that all sounds well divided. Let's speak again in a fortnight.
Sounds good, thank you.
That is the end of Section Three. Now turn to Section Four.
